newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: POLICE GIVE ARNOTT'S EXTORTIONIST DEADLINE
Senior police from New South Wales and Queensland have called on the Arnotts extortionists to withdraw their threats, and have given them until Monday to make contact.
Queensland Detective Superintendent Ron Pickering told a packed media conference in Brisbane a short time ago that if that doesn't happen they'll consider the threat to be over.
But he says the hunt for the extortionists will continue.
New South Wales Assistant Police Commissioner Clive Small reiterated the call, saying police will not give in.
Arnotts managing-director Chris Roberts says no decision has been made as to whether Arnotts' products will go back on the shelves after Monday.
The extortionists want four New South Wales detectives, who gave evidence at a Brisbane murder trial, to take a public lie-detector test.
JAPANESE CRIME GROUPS ACTIVE IN AUSTRALIA
The National Crime Authority says it's uncovered evidence of activity in Australia by Japanese mafia gangs.
But it says it can't investigate further without approval from State and Federal Governments.
A confidential NCA report, part of which is on the Internet, says a group called the Boryokudan tried to obtain a casino licence in Canberra, but the attempt was detected and failed.
The report warns that the group's activities are likely to increase in Australia.
It also probed other Japanese groups, finding the biggest threats to be money laundering and investment.
There's also evidence in the report that Australian women are being recruited to work as prostitutes in Japan.
INTERNATIONAL DEFENCE ALLIANCE MEANS JOBS
Australia's first high technology defence company, the result of an alliance between firms in the U-S and Australia, is set to produce advanced software systems here and in South East Asia.
Lockheed Martin and Australia's Transfield Defence Systems are behind the new company, which is yet to be named, but is expected to create a-thousand jobs in Melbourne, where it will be based.
The new company's already won a 900-million dollar contract to manage the Jindalee Operational Radar Network.
Victorian Industry Minister, Mark Birrell, described the move as a great breakthrough for Melbourne, because it will enable Victoria to get into advanced manufacturing.
Mr Birrell described the company's decision to base itself in Melbourne as a coup for the city.
FORMER CHIEF JUSTICE ON HIGH COURT CHANGE
The Former Chief Justice of the High Court, Sir Harry Gibbs, says there's room for the states to be given a more formal role in choosing High Court judges.
But Sir Harry has rejected other suggestions by the Queensland Premier, Rob Borbidge, for changes to the High Court, including a 10 year maximum term for judges.
Sir Harry says fixed-term appointments have been regarded as having the potential to weaken the judiciary's independence, and he wouldn't like to revert to them.
Mr Borbidge's suggestions have been sparked by his anger over the High Court's recent Wik decision that pastoral leases and Native Title can co-exist.
PROFESSOR ATTACKS REFUSAL TO APPOINT FUNDER TO SCIENCE POST
An eminent researcher says it's very regrettable that the balance of power in the Senate should influence an appointment to a top science position.
The Federal Government has decided not to proceed with the appointment of Professor John Funder to head the National Health and Medical Research Council.
It's been widely speculated Independent Senator Brian Harradine opposed the appointment because of Professor Funder's support for the release of the abortion drug RU 486.

Former University of Melbourne Vice-Chancellor, Professor David Pennington, says Professor Funder's an eminent scientist who doesn't allow his personal views to interfere with his job. He says it's very regrettable that the decision might have been influenced by whether or not Senator Harradine will support the government in other areas.
Federal Health minister Michael Wooldridge has announced the new head of the NHMRC is Professor Richard Larkins, who's currently Professor of Medicine at the University of Melbourne.
FORMER LABOR MINISTER DUMPED FROM MEAT CORPORATION
Former Labor Minister John Kerin says the Federal Government should have kept him on as Chairman of the Meat and Livestock Corporation in the lead up to a restructure of the industry.
Mr Kerin says the Government's decision not to extend his appointment was straight politics.
He says a new board will be appointed as part of the new structure, and for the sake of the industry, it would have made sense to keep him on as chairman in the intervening period.
Primary Industries minister, John Anderson, is understood to have wanted Mr Kerin to be kept on.
HEAT KNOCKING MELBURNITES FOR SIX
Ambulance officers in Melbourne are warning children and people who are elderly or ill to avoid the heat if they can.
Paramedic, Steve Wood, says four people have collapsed in Melbourne so far, due to the heatwave.
Mr Wood says more people are expected to feel the heat as the day wears on.
He says people should avoid excessive exercise and keep their fluid intake up.
